cards.nota: Clássico falso amigo. 'Embarazada' = grávida. Envergonhada = 'avergonzada'.
cards.notaEn: 'Embarazada' means pregnant. To say you are embarrassed, use 'avergonzado' or turn it around with 'me da vergüenza'.

cards.nota: 'Exquisito' é elogio: delicioso, requintado. Esquisito = 'raro' ou 'extraño'.
cards.notaEn: 'Exquisito' is praise, above all at the table: '¡Está exquisito!' is what you say when a meal is superb. It also covers refined taste or manners. Something strange is 'raro' or 'extraño'.

cards.nota: 'Espera un rato' = espera um pouquinho. O animal rato = 'ratón'.
cards.notaEn: 'Espera un rato' = wait a while. It looks like 'rat' and is not: the animal is 'una rata', and the small one is 'un ratón'.

cards.nota: 'Borracho' = bêbado. Borracha de apagar = 'goma de borrar'.
cards.notaEn: 'Borracho' = drunk. Keep it apart from 'borroso' (blurry) and 'borrado' (erased), which come from 'borrar', to rub out.

cards.nota: 'Oficina' = escritório. Oficina mecânica = 'taller'.
cards.notaEn: 'La oficina' is the office where people work at desks. The place a car gets fixed is 'el taller', and a factory is 'la fábrica'.

cards.nota: 'Taller' = oficina, ateliê, também workshop. Talher = 'cubierto'.
cards.notaEn: 'Taller' covers the mechanic's garage, an artist's studio and a hands-on training workshop. It has nothing to do with height — taller in that sense is 'más alto'.

cards.nota: 'Cachorro' = filhote (de qualquer animal). Cachorro (cão) = 'perro'.
cards.notaEn: 'Cachorro' is the young of an animal — a puppy, a cub, a pup. A grown dog is 'el perro'.

cards.nota: 'Polvo' = pó/poeira. O animal polvo = 'pulpo'.
cards.notaEn: 'Polvo' is dust on a shelf, or powder in a recipe. The octopus is 'el pulpo' — one letter apart, and easy to swap by accident.

cards.nota: 'Cena' = jantar; 'cenar' = jantar (verbo). Cena de filme = 'escena'.
cards.notaEn: 'La cena' is dinner, the evening meal, and 'cenar' is the verb that goes with it. Mind the neighbours: 'la escena' is a scene and 'la ceniza' is ash.

cards.nota: 'Escoba' = vassoura. Escova = 'cepillo'.
cards.notaEn: 'Escoba' = broom. Its neighbours in the cupboard: 'el cepillo' is a brush, 'la fregona' the mop, 'el recogedor' the dustpan.

cards.nota: 'Cola' = rabo/cauda e também fila ('hacer cola'). Cola de colar = 'pegamento'.
cards.notaEn: 'Cola' is both a tail and a queue — 'hacer cola' is to queue up, or to stand in line. Glue is 'el pegamento'.

cards.nota: 'Vaso' = copo. Vaso de flores = 'jarrón' ou 'florero'.
cards.notaEn: 'Un vaso de agua' is a glass of water. A vase for flowers is 'un jarrón' or 'un florero', and a wine glass is 'una copa'.

cards.nota: 'Largo' = comprido. Largo (em largura) = 'ancho'.
cards.notaEn: 'Largo' means long, in extension. Large in size is 'grande'; wide is 'ancho'. The pair 'largo/ancho' is length against width.

cards.nota: Par do anterior: 'ancho' = largo; 'largo' = comprido.
cards.notaEn: 'Ancho' is wide — width, not length. Length is 'largo'. The nouns are 'la anchura' and 'la longitud'.

cards.nota: 'Brincar' = pular. Brincar = 'jugar'.
cards.notaEn: 'Brincar' is to jump or leap: 'el niño brincaba de alegría'. To play is 'jugar' — a different verb altogether.

cards.nota: 'Apellido' = sobrenome. Apelido = 'apodo' ou 'sobrenombre'.
cards.notaEn: 'Apellido' is the family name. In Spain and much of Latin America people carry two: the father's first, then the mother's. A nickname is 'un apodo'.

cards.nota: 'Propina' = gorjeta. Propina/suborno = 'soborno'.
cards.notaEn: 'La propina' is the tip you leave for service. A bribe is 'un soborno' — a very different transaction. In Spain tipping is modest and often skipped.

cards.nota: 'El presunto asesino' = o suposto assassino. Presunto (comida) = 'jamón'.
cards.notaEn: 'El presunto asesino' is the alleged killer — the word the police and the papers use before a conviction. It comes from 'presumir', to presume.

cards.nota: 'Crianza' = criação/educação. Criança = 'niño' ou 'niña'.
cards.notaEn: 'La crianza' is the raising of a child — how someone was brought up. It also names the ageing of wine: 'un vino de crianza'. The verb is 'criar'.

cards.nota: 'Aula' = sala. Aula (lição) = 'clase'.
cards.notaEn: 'El aula' is the room, not the lesson — a lesson is 'una clase'. Mind the article: 'aula' is feminine but takes 'el' in the singular, because it opens with a stressed a. Plural, 'las aulas'.

cards.nota: 'Me acuerdo de ti' = lembro de você. Acordar = 'despertarse'.
cards.notaEn: 'Me acuerdo de ti' = I remember you. It is reflexive and takes 'de'. Keep it apart from 'despertarse', to wake up, and from plain 'acordar', to agree on something.

cards.nota: 'Todavía no' = ainda não. Todavia (contudo) = 'sin embargo'.
cards.notaEn: 'Todavía' = still, and 'todavía no' = not yet. Its opposite number is 'ya': 'ya llegó' (he's here already) against 'todavía no llega'.

cards.nota: 'Hasta luego' = até mais. Não é 'logo' no sentido de imediatamente.
cards.notaEn: 'Hasta luego' is the everyday goodbye — see you later. It is not immediate: right away is 'ahora mismo' or 'enseguida'. In writing, 'luego' can also mean therefore.

cards.nota: 'No hay sitio' = não tem lugar. Site = 'sitio web' ou 'página web'.
cards.notaEn: 'No hay sitio' = there's no room. A website is 'un sitio web', the one place the English sense survives. 'Sitio' also means a siege, as in 'el sitio de Numancia'.

cards.nota: 'Salsa' = molho. A erva salsa = 'perejil'.
cards.notaEn: 'La salsa' is any sauce — 'salsa de tomate', 'salsa verde'. The herb parsley is 'el perejil'. And yes, it is also the music and the dance.

cards.nota: 'Zurdo' = canhoto. Surdo = 'sordo'.
cards.notaEn: 'Zurdo' = left-handed; the right-handed one is 'diestro'. Careful with 'sordo', deaf, which sits one letter away.

cards.nota: 'Cadera' = quadril. Cadeira = 'silla'.
cards.notaEn: 'La cadera' is the hip — the joint, and the shelf you rest a child on. The waist just above it is 'la cintura'.

cards.nota: Tem os dois sentidos: a parte do braço e o brinquedo.
cards.notaEn: 'Muñeca' carries both: the wrist on your arm and a doll to play with. 'Me duele la muñeca' or 'una muñeca de trapo' — same word, and no thread joining them.

cards.nota: 'Estoy enfadado' = estou bravo. Na América Latina usa-se mais 'enojado'.
cards.notaEn: 'Estoy enfadado' = I'm angry. In Spain that is the everyday word; across Latin America you will hear 'enojado' far more often.

cards.nota: 'Quítate de ahí' = sai daí. Quitar dívida = 'saldar' ou 'liquidar'.
cards.notaEn: 'Quítate de ahí' = get out of the way. 'Quitar' is to take away or take off: 'quítate el abrigo', take off your coat. Reflexive, 'quitarse' is what you do to your own clothes.

cards.nota: Na porta, 'tirar' = puxar e 'empujar' = empurrar. Tirar (remover) = 'quitar'.
cards.notaEn: On a door, 'tirar' means pull and 'empujar' means push — worth learning before you shove. Elsewhere it is to throw away: 'tira eso a la basura'.

cards.nota: Tela de pintura = 'lienzo'. Cuidado para não confundir com 'pantalón'.
cards.notaEn: 'La pantalla' is the screen — of a phone, a television, or a cinema. Keep it apart from 'el pantalón', trousers, which it echoes. A painter's canvas is 'un lienzo'.

cards.nota: Assinatura (rubrica) = 'firma'.
cards.notaEn: 'La asignatura' is a school or university subject. 'Asignatura pendiente' is one you still have to pass — and, figuratively, any unfinished business. A signature is 'una firma'.

distratores: o carro de corrida / o automóvel
cards.nota: 'Estudio la carrera de Derecho' = curso Direito.
cards.notaEn: 'Estudio la carrera de Derecho' = I'm doing a law degree. It is also a race: 'una carrera de caballos'. A career in the English sense is closer to 'la trayectoria profesional'.

distratoresEn: the box office / the ticket queue
cards.nota: 'Billete de tren' = passagem de trem; 'billete de 50 euros' = nota de 50.
cards.notaEn: 'Billete de tren' is a train ticket; 'billete de 50 euros' is a fifty-euro note. Across much of Latin America the travel ticket is 'el boleto' instead.

cards.nota: 'A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda' = Deus ajuda quem cedo madruga.
cards.notaEn: 'A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda' — God helps the one who rises early. The noun is 'la madrugada', the small hours before dawn.

cards.nota: Oposto de 'madrugar'.
cards.notaEn: The opposite of 'madrugar'. 'Anoche trasnoché' = I was up all night. Someone who makes a habit of it is 'un trasnochador'.

cards.nota: Pessoa que sente muito frio. Na América Latina: 'friolento'.
cards.notaEn: 'Friolero' describes the person, not the weather: someone who feels the cold badly. 'Soy muy friolera' = I'm always cold. Across Latin America, 'friolento'.

cards.nota: Também se usa para pessoas melosas demais.
cards.notaEn: 'Empalagoso' is too sweet to finish — the cake that defeats you halfway. It also describes a person who is cloying, all sugar and no substance.

cards.nota: Vale para comida e para pessoas: 'es un chico soso' = é um cara sem graça.
cards.notaEn: 'Soso' is unsalted, and by extension dull: 'es un chico soso' is he's a bit of a bore. At the table its opposite is 'salado'.

cards.nota: 'Un bar cutre' = um bar caindo aos pedaços. Também: sovina.
cards.notaEn: 'Un bar cutre' is a dive — grimy, cheap, coming apart. Of a person it means stingy. Very Spanish, and always dismissive.

cards.nota: 'El curro' = o trampo. Muito comum na Espanha.
cards.notaEn: Spanish slang for working: 'me voy al curro' = I'm off to work. 'El curro' is the job itself. Standard Spanish is 'trabajar'.

cards.nota: 'Es muy maja' = ela é muito gente boa.
cards.notaEn: 'Es muy maja' = she's really nice. Heard all over Spain for someone pleasant and easy to be around; it can also mean good-looking.

cards.nota: 'Un amigo entrañable' = um amigo muito querido.
cards.notaEn: 'Un amigo entrañable' is a friend held deep inside — from 'las entrañas', the guts. Warmer and more intimate than plain 'querido'.

cards.nota: Sinônimo mais coloquial: 'echar de menos'.
cards.notaEn: 'Añoro mi casa' = I miss home. It leans literary and wistful; day to day you will hear 'echar de menos', or 'extrañar' in Latin America.

cards.nota: Falso amigo. A sobremesa (doce) = 'el postre'.
cards.notaEn: 'La sobremesa' is the stretch of talk that keeps everyone at the table long after the plates are cleared — an institution in Spain. Dessert is 'el postre'.

cards.en: to use for the first time
aceitasEn: to use for the first time
to wear for the first time
cards.nota: 'Estreno zapatos' = estou usando sapatos novos pela primeira vez.
cards.notaEn: 'Estreno zapatos' = I'm wearing these shoes for the first time. It is also what a film does on opening night: 'la película se estrena mañana'.

cards.nota: 'Ya me las apañaré' = eu me viro.
cards.notaEn: 'Ya me las apañaré' = I'll manage. Always with 'las' stuck to the end, and it comes with a shrug: whatever it takes, I'll sort it out.

distratores: a chapa / a placa de metal
o chapéu / a aba de palha
cards.nota: Também pode significar 'bico', trabalho pequeno.
cards.notaEn: 'Vaya chapuza' = what a mess of a job. It can also mean a small odd job on the side, and the person who does them is 'un chapuzas'.

cards.nota: Pessoa que se ofende ou reclama de coisinhas.
cards.notaEn: 'Quisquilloso' is the person who takes offence at nothing and picks at details. 'No seas quisquilloso' = don't be so touchy.

cards.nota: Sinônimos: 'terco', 'cabezota'.
cards.notaEn: 'Tozudo' = stubborn, and rarely a compliment. Its companions are 'terco' and, more colloquially, 'cabezota' — big-headed in the mule sense.

cards.nota: Falta de cuidado e de vontade de fazer as coisas.
cards.notaEn: 'La desidia' is neglect born of not caring enough to act — apathy with consequences. 'La desidia de las autoridades' is standard newspaper Spanish.

cards.nota: 'La producción ha mermado' = a produção diminuiu.
cards.notaEn: 'La producción ha mermado' = output has fallen. It suggests loss by wearing away rather than a sudden drop. The noun 'la merma' is the shortfall itself.

cards.nota: 'Socavar la confianza' = minar a confiança.
cards.notaEn: 'Socavar la confianza' = to undermine trust. Literally it is to dig away underneath until the thing gives; the figurative sense is the common one.

cards.nota: 'Soslayar el problema' = fugir do problema. 'De soslayo' = de esguelha.
cards.notaEn: 'Soslayar el problema' = to dodge the problem. From 'de soslayo', sideways — the glance you give something without turning your head.

cards.nota: 'No es asunto baladí' = não é assunto de somenos importância.
cards.notaEn: 'No es asunto baladí' = it's no trifling matter — and it turns up far more often in the negative than in the positive. An Arabic borrowing, from 'baladi', local or homegrown.

cards.nota: 'Prueba fehaciente' = prova cabal. Comum na linguagem jurídica.
cards.notaEn: 'Prueba fehaciente' = conclusive proof. Legal and formal register, built from 'fe' (faith) and 'hacer' — something that makes you believe.

cards.nota: 'Plazo perentorio' = prazo improrrogável.
cards.notaEn: 'Plazo perentorio' = a deadline that will not be extended. Legal and formal, carrying both urgency and finality: once it passes, the right is gone.

cards.nota: 'Ni un atisbo de duda' = nem uma sombra de dúvida.
cards.notaEn: 'Ni un atisbo de duda' = not a shadow of a doubt. An 'atisbo' is the first faint sign of something, from 'atisbar', to catch sight of.

cards.nota: Vem de 'zozobrar' (naufragar): a angústia de quem está prestes a afundar.
cards.notaEn: From 'zozobrar', to capsize: 'la zozobra' is the anguish of someone about to go under. Heavier and more literary than plain 'angustia'.

cards.nota: 'Hacinamiento carcelario' = superlotação carcerária.
cards.notaEn: 'Hacinamiento carcelario' = prison overcrowding. From 'hacinar', to pile up — people stacked into a space too small for them.

cards.nota: 'En menoscabo de' = em detrimento de.
cards.notaEn: 'En menoscabo de' = to the detriment of. It names damage that reduces something's worth or standing — a property's value, a person's reputation.

cards.nota: 'Pergeñar un plan' = bolar um plano às pressas.
cards.notaEn: 'Pergeñar un plan' = to throw a plan together. The word hints that it was done quickly and roughly, which is half its charm.

cards.nota: 'Hizo ademán de irse' = fez menção de ir embora.
cards.notaEn: 'Hizo ademán de irse' = he made as if to leave. An 'ademán' is a movement of the body that signals intent, often one that stops short of the act.

cards.nota: 'Libre albedrío' = livre-arbítrio.
cards.notaEn: 'Libre albedrío' = free will, the term used in theology and philosophy. On its own, 'a su albedrío' means as one pleases, at one's own discretion.

cards.nota: Usado também para obras horríveis: 'un engendro de película'.
cards.notaEn: 'Un engendro' is something misshapen — a freak, or by extension an awful piece of work: 'un engendro de película'. From 'engendrar', to beget.

cards.pt: perder o sono / não conseguir dormir
distratores: velar um morto / passar a noite ao lado
cards.nota: Dois sentidos: não conseguir dormir e dedicar-se muito a alguém.
cards.notaEn: Two senses. 'Me desvelé anoche' = I lay awake all night. And 'desvelarse por alguien' is to put yourself out for someone, losing sleep over them.

cards.nota: 'Me pilló mintiendo' = me flagrou mentindo. '¿Lo pillas?' = tá sacando?
cards.notaEn: 'Me pilló mintiendo' = he caught me lying. Spanish slang, and it stretches: '¿lo pillas?' is do you get it, and 'me pilla lejos' is it's out of my way.

cards.pt: o entardecer / o pôr do sol
distratores: o amanhecer / o nascer do sol
a madrugada / o meio da noite
o meio-dia / o sol a pino
o atraso / a demora na chegada
cards.nota: 'Al atardecer' = ao entardecer.
cards.notaEn: 'Al atardecer' = at dusk, as the light goes. Built like its neighbours: 'el amanecer' is daybreak, 'el anochecer' is nightfall.

cards.nota: 'Ufano de sus logros' = orgulhoso de suas conquistas.
cards.notaEn: 'Ufano de sus logros' = proud of his achievements. The pride is visible and a little puffed up — pleased with oneself, and showing it.

aceitasEn: it makes no difference to me
its all the same to me
it is all the same to me
cards.nota: Variante: 'me da lo mismo'.
cards.notaEn: 'Me da igual' = I don't mind, either way. Variant: 'me da lo mismo'. Said flatly enough, it tips over into I couldn't care less.

distratores: Nada passa por aqui. / Está parado.
Nada acontece nunca. / É sempre igual.
Não vai dar certo. / Vai falhar.
Não passe por aí. / Evite o lugar.
cards.nota: Resposta padrão quando alguém pede desculpas.
cards.notaEn: The standard reply when someone apologises: no harm done. It also works as plain reassurance — 'no pasa nada, seguimos'.

cards.pt: Estou de saco cheio de esperar.
aceitas: estou de saco cheio de esperar
to de saco cheio de esperar
aceitasEn: i m fed up with waiting
i am fed up with waiting
distratoresEn: I am full of food now.
I hope to eat my fill.
I am willing to wait longer.
I have plenty of time to wait.
cards.nota: 'Estar harto de' = estar de saco cheio de.
cards.notaEn: 'Estar harto de' = to be fed up with. Literally to be stuffed, and the food sense is still alive: 'me harté de paella'.

cards.pt: Me dá uma mão. / Me ajuda.
aceitasEn: give me a hand with this
distratores: Me jogue a mão. / Me arremesse.
Solte a minha mão. / Me largue.
Levante a mão. / Peça a palavra.
Me dê a mão. / Vamos atravessar.
cards.nota: 'Echar una mano' = dar uma ajuda.
cards.notaEn: 'Echar una mano' = to lend a hand. 'Echar' is the workhorse verb for throwing or putting, and it turns up in dozens of set phrases.

cards.nota: Construção com 'se me' muito comum em espanhol.
cards.notaEn: The 'se me' construction puts the event beyond your control — it is getting late on me. Same shape as 'se me olvidó' (I forgot) and 'se me cayó' (I dropped it).

cards.pt: De jeito nenhum. / Nem a pau.
distratores: Nem de brincadeira. / Sem graça nenhuma.
Nem que fosse grátis. / Não vale a pena.
cards.nota: Vulgar-ish na Espanha. Versão neutra: 'ni de broma', 'ni hablar'.
cards.notaEn: Emphatic refusal, and a shade crude in Spain. The neutral versions are 'ni de broma' and 'ni hablar'. 'De coña' on its own means as a joke.

cards.en: He has his head in the clouds.
aceitasEn: he has his head in the clouds
hes got his head in the clouds
distratores: Está com a cabeça nas alturas do sucesso.
distratoresEn: He is flying on a plane.
He is riding high on success.
cards.nota: Sinônimo: 'estar en Babia'.
cards.notaEn: 'Estar en las nubes' = to be off with your thoughts, not paying attention. Its Spanish twin is 'estar en Babia'.

cards.pt: Me parece familiar. / Já ouvi isso.
distratores: Toca para mim. / Faça um som.
cards.nota: 'No me suena' = nunca ouvi falar.
cards.notaEn: 'Me suena' = it rings a bell. The negative is the more useful one: 'no me suena' = never heard of it.

cards.nota: 'A lo mejor' + indicativo = talvez. Já 'quizás' costuma pedir subjuntivo.
cards.notaEn: 'A lo mejor' means maybe and — unlike 'quizás' or 'tal vez' — it takes the indicative, never the subjunctive: 'a lo mejor viene', not 'venga'.

aceitas: faz dois anos que estou aqui
ha dois anos que moro aqui
tem dois anos que estou aqui
aceitasEn: i ve been here two years
i have been here two years
ive been here for two years
i have been here for two years
distratores: Passei por aqui há dois anos.
distratoresEn: I take two years from here.
It will take me two years.
I came by here two years ago.
cards.nota: 'Llevar + tempo' é o jeito espanhol de dizer 'estar há'.
cards.notaEn: 'Llevar + time' is how Spanish says how long something has been going on: 'llevo dos años aquí', 'lleva una hora esperando'. English reaches for the present perfect; Spanish stays in the present.

cards.nota: 'Acabar de + infinitivo' = acabar de fazer algo.
cards.notaEn: 'Acabar de + infinitive' = to have just done something. In the present it means the action is barely over: 'acabo de comer', I've just eaten.

cards.pt: Eu simpatizo com ele. / Acho ele gente boa.
cards.en: I get on well with him.
aceitasEn: i get on well with him
i get along well with him
distratores: Ele caiu bem. / A roupa ficou boa.
Ele caiu em cima de mim. / Me derrubou.
Eu caio bem ali. / O lugar me serve.
Ele me faz bem. / Melhora minha saúde.
distratoresEn: He is good for my health.
cards.nota: 'Caer bien/mal' fala de simpatia, não de amor. 'Me gusta' pode soar romântico.
cards.notaEn: 'Caer bien' is about liking someone as a person. Keep it apart from 'me gusta', which about a person reads as attraction. The opposite is 'me cae mal'.

cards.pt: Dar uma mancada. / Pisar na bola.
cards.en: To put your foot in it.
aceitasEn: to put your foot in it
to put ones foot in it
distratores: Meter o pé na porta. / Forçar a entrada.
Enfiar o pé na jaca. / Exagerar na bebida.
Botar a pata no chão. / Firmar o passo.
Bater o pé. / Insistir na teimosia.
distratoresEn: To get your foot in the door.
cards.nota: 'Metí la pata' = falei/fiz besteira.
cards.notaEn: 'Metí la pata' = I put my foot in it, I said the wrong thing. 'La pata' is an animal's leg, which makes the picture clumsier still.

cards.pt: Ficar no fim do mundo. / Ser longe pra caramba.
cards.en: To be in the middle of nowhere.
aceitasEn: to be in the middle of nowhere
to be out in the sticks
to be in the back of beyond
to be a long way out
distratores: Estar no quinto andar. / Subir mais um pouco.
Estar entre os pinheiros. / Ficar dentro da mata.
Estar em quinto lugar. / Quase chegar ao pódio.
Estar bem no ponto certo. / Acertar o alvo.
distratoresEn: To be up on the fifth floor.
To be deep inside the pine wood.
To be in fifth place overall.
To be exactly on the right spot.
cards.nota: Sinônimo: 'en el quinto infierno', 'donde Cristo perdió el gorro'.
cards.notaEn: 'Vive en el quinto pino' = he lives miles out. Spain has funnier versions of the same idea: 'en el quinto infierno', 'donde Cristo perdió el gorro'.

distratores: Estender a toalha. / Secar ao sol.
Lavar a roupa suja. / Brigar em casa.
cards.nota: Cuidado: 'tirar' aqui é jogar, não puxar.
cards.notaEn: The same image as in English, straight from boxing. Mind the verb: here 'tirar' is to throw, though on a door the very same word means pull.

cards.es: No tiene pelos en la lengua.
aceitasEn: he does not mince his words
he doesn t mince his words
he tells it like it is
distratoresEn: He never says anything at all.
He talks nineteen to the dozen.
cards.nota: Diz o que pensa sem filtro.
cards.notaEn: 'No tener pelos en la lengua' = to say what you think without softening it. The picture is a tongue with nothing in the way.

aceitasEn: it s a piece of cake
it is a piece of cake
cards.nota: Equivale a 'é canja'.
cards.notaEn: 'Es pan comido' = it's bread already eaten, so there's no effort left in it. English reaches for cake, Spanish for bread.

cards.es: Cuesta un ojo de la cara.
cards.en: It costs an arm and a leg.
aceitasEn: it costs an arm and a leg
costs an arm and a leg
distratoresEn: It gives you a black eye.
It is well worth a look.
cards.nota: Quase idêntica ao português, mas no singular: 'un ojo'.
cards.notaEn: Spanish pays with an eye where English pays with an arm and a leg: 'cuesta un ojo de la cara'. Note the singular — one eye, not both.

cards.notaEn: 'De buenas a primeras' = with no warning and no run-up. It often carries a hint of complaint: you sprang it on me.

cards.notaEn: 'Montar un pollo' = to kick up a fuss in public. Very Spanish. 'Montar' here is to stage or set up; the chicken is anyone's guess.

cards.notaEn: 'Me importa un pepino' = it matters to me about as much as a cucumber does. Swap the vegetable freely: 'un pimiento', 'un rábano', 'un comino'.

cards.notaEn: 'Hacerse el sueco' = to pretend you didn't hear or didn't understand. The 'sueco' is probably not the Swede but 'soccus', the clown's shoe of Roman comedy.

cards.nota: Cumprimento informal padrão.
cards.notaEn: The standard informal greeting. '¿Qué tal?' on its own is how are you; put a noun after it and it asks how something went: '¿qué tal el viaje?'

aceitasEn: i feel like going to sleep
im in the mood to sleep
distratoresEn: I have to go to sleep.
cards.nota: 'Tener ganas de' = estar com vontade de.
cards.notaEn: 'Tener ganas de' + infinitive = to feel like doing something. 'Las ganas' are the urge itself: 'me quedé con las ganas' means I never got to.

distratoresEn: It has been cold for ages.
cards.nota: Clima em espanhol usa 'hacer': 'hace calor', 'hace sol'.
cards.notaEn: Spanish weather runs on 'hacer': 'hace frío', 'hace calor', 'hace sol'. Careful — 'tengo frío' is about you, not the weather: I'm cold.

cards.nota: 'Irse' (pronominal) = ir embora; 'ir' = ir a um lugar.
cards.notaEn: 'Irse' is to leave, to go away; plain 'ir' is to go somewhere. 'Me voy' = I'm off. 'Voy' = I'm on my way there.

cards.nota: O espanhol prefere a forma 'se me olvidó' (o esquecimento 'aconteceu' comigo).
cards.notaEn: Spanish prefers 'se me olvidó' — the forgetting happened to me — over plain 'olvidé'. The construction spreads the blame around, and it is everywhere: 'se me cayó', 'se me rompió'.

distratores: Faltam dois para mim. / Preciso de dois.
Dei dois embora. / Me livrei deles.
cards.nota: 'Quedar' com pronome = restar, sobrar.
cards.notaEn: 'Quedar' with an indirect pronoun means to be left over: 'me quedan dos'. Without the pronoun, 'quedarse' is to stay: 'me quedo aquí'.

cards.pt: Está para chegar a qualquer momento.
distratores: Está caindo no chão neste momento.
Vai cair de um momento para outro.

Está prestes a desistir de tudo.

He is about to give up.
cards.nota: Usado para algo iminente: pessoa, notícia, evento.
cards.notaEn: 'Estar al caer' = to be imminent — a person about to arrive, news about to break. 'Al + infinitive' generally marks the moment of an action: 'al llegar', on arriving.

not that i am aware of
as far as i know no

cards.notaEn: 'Que yo sepa' takes the subjunctive and hedges whatever follows: as far as I know. It works on its own too — '¿vino? Que yo sepa, no.'

Vou ver você amanhã sem falta.

We are looking at each other now.
Let's watch the film together today.
I will see you tomorrow for sure.
cards.nota: Despedida vaga e amistosa, muito comum.
cards.notaEn: A warm, vague goodbye — nobody is committing to a date. 'A ver si' + subjunctive is the standard way to float a loose intention.

distratoresEn: I hope he arrives early tomorrow.
He said he would come tomorrow.
If only he had come yesterday.
cards.nota: 'Ojalá' + imperfeito do subjuntivo é desejo pouco provável; com o presente ('venga'), desejo plausível. Em português o par não é simétrico: 'tomara' é forma fossilizada (antigo mais-que-perfeito de 'tomar') e praticamente só admite presente do subjuntivo — 'tomara que ele venha' é natural, 'tomara que ele viesse' soa estranho. O desejo improvável sai por outro caminho: 'quem me dera que ele viesse', 'se ao menos ele viesse', 'eu queria que ele viesse' ou 'oxalá ele viesse' (mais literário, e cognato direto de 'ojalá' — ambos vêm do árabe law šāʾ Allāh).
cards.notaEn: 'Ojalá' + imperfect subjunctive is the wish you don't expect to be granted: if only. Swap in the present subjunctive — 'ojalá venga mañana' — and it becomes a real hope. The word is Arabic, from 'law šāʾ Allāh', if God wills.

cards.es: De haberlo sabido, no habría venido.

On finding out, I do not come.
I did not know and did not come.
cards.nota: 'De + infinitivo composto' equivale a uma condicional: 'si lo hubiera sabido'.
cards.notaEn: 'De + perfect infinitive' is a compact conditional, equal to 'si lo hubiera sabido'. Formal and rather elegant; you will meet it in writing more than in speech.

cards.es: Por más que lo intente, no lo logra.

He will only manage it if he tries again.

He does not try, and so he does not manage.
cards.nota: 'Lograr' = conseguir, alcançar.
cards.notaEn: 'Por más que' + subjunctive = however much, no matter how much. 'Lograr' is to manage or achieve, and it takes the thing achieved directly: 'lo logró'.

cards.nota: 'Como si' sempre pede imperfeito ou mais-que-perfeito do subjuntivo.
cards.notaEn: 'Como si' always takes the imperfect or the pluperfect subjunctive, never the present — 'como si fuera', 'como si hubiera pasado'. There is no exception worth learning.

Even though it rained, I went.
cards.nota: 'Aunque' + subjuntivo = concessão hipotética; + indicativo = fato conhecido.
cards.notaEn: 'Aunque' + subjunctive = even if, a hypothesis. 'Aunque' + indicative = even though, a known fact: 'aunque llueve, iré' means it is raining and I'm going anyway.

cards.notaEn: 'Le lo' is impossible in Spanish, so the indirect pronoun turns into 'se': 'se lo dije'. Indirect always comes before direct.

cards.notaEn: 'Llevar + time + gerund' describes something still going on: 'llevo tres años estudiando'. Spanish holds it in the present where English needs a perfect.

cards.notaEn: A double negative that means the opposite of how it looks: there is no misfortune that does not arrive for some good. Common in speech, usually as consolation.

Early to bed, early to rise.

Good things come to those who wait.
cards.nota: Mesma ideia do provérbio português.
cards.notaEn: Literally, God helps the one who rises early. English swaps God for a bird, but the moral is identical: get up and get going.

cards.nota: Sobre querer fazer coisas demais ao mesmo tempo.
cards.notaEn: 'Abarcar' is to take in or encompass; 'apretar' is to grip tight. Reach for too much and you hold none of it firmly.

cards.notaEn: 'Dar gato por liebre' = to pass off cat as hare, selling someone something worse than what was promised. The image is old; the complaint is still current.

distratores: São parentes. / Têm o mesmo sangue.
cards.nota: Amizade muito próxima.
cards.notaEn: 'Uña y carne' — nail and flesh, which you cannot pull apart without hurting both. Said of friends who are always together.

cards.notaEn: 'Andarse por las ramas' = to wander off into the branches instead of going for the trunk. Its opposite is 'ir al grano'.

cards.notaEn: 'Salirse con la suya' = to get one's own way, usually against opposition. 'La suya' stands in for 'su voluntad' — his will, left unspoken.

cards.notaEn: 'Quedarse de piedra' = to be turned to stone by surprise. 'Quedarse' + adjective is a whole family: 'me quedé helado', 'se quedó en blanco'.

distratoresEn: I am off sick from work.
cards.nota: 'Bajón' = queda de ânimo.
cards.notaEn: 'Un bajón' is a sudden drop — in mood, in energy, in blood sugar. 'Me dio un bajón' = I suddenly crashed.

to add fuel to the flames
to pour petrol on the fire

To cook over a wood fire.
cards.nota: Agravar um conflito de propósito.
cards.notaEn: 'Echar leña al fuego' = to throw firewood on the fire, making a quarrel worse on purpose.

He did it during the night.
cards.nota: Sem ordem nem critério.
cards.notaEn: 'A troche y moche' = wildly, with no order and no judgement. Neither word means anything on its own any more; the phrase carries the whole sense.

cards.nota: Insistência obstinada em algo.
cards.notaEn: 'Erre que erre' — the rolled R repeated over and over, like someone who will not stop. It marks obstinate, wearying insistence.

cards.en: I only just managed to finish.

i scraped through to the end

cards.nota: 'A duras penas' = com muita dificuldade.
cards.notaEn: 'A duras penas' = barely, with great difficulty. 'Las penas' here are hardships rather than sorrows.

distratores: Que nojo! / Não dá para olhar!

cards.notaEn: 'Ser la leche' can go either way: astonishing good or astonishing bad. Tone and context carry the whole meaning — 'este tío es la leche' could be praise or despair.

cards.notaEn: 'Quedar' here is to arrange to meet: 'hemos quedado a las ocho'. 'Vale' is the all-purpose OK in Spain — in Latin America you would hear 'listo', 'dale' or 'bueno'.

aceitasEn: its a good thing you arrived
distratoresEn: It is worse that you arrived.

cards.notaEn: 'Menos mal que' = thank goodness, just as well. Literally less bad, and it always introduces relief at a near miss.

cards.nota: 'Salir a la calle' = sair na rua. Cuidado com a pronúncia do 'll'.
cards.notaEn: 'Salir a la calle' = to go outside. Mind the 'll' — in most of Spain it sounds like the y in yes; in Argentina it turns into a sh.

cards.nota: Do mesmo grupo: 'puerta' = porta, 'pared' = parede.
cards.notaEn: House vocabulary travels in packs: 'la puerta' is the door, 'la pared' the wall, 'el techo' the ceiling. A shop window is 'el escaparate'.

cards.nota: Cuidado: 'suelo' também é a forma de 'soler' (costumar) na primeira pessoa.
cards.notaEn: 'El suelo' is the floor indoors and the ground outside. It is also the first person of 'soler': 'suelo ir' = I usually go.

cards.nota: O 'll' espanhol soa como o nosso 'lh' ou 'j', dependendo da região.
cards.notaEn: 'La llave' is the key, and across much of Latin America the tap as well. 'Echar la llave' = to lock up.

cards.nota: Também significa barraca de acampar: 'tienda de campaña'.
cards.notaEn: 'La tienda' is the shop, and also the tent you camp in: 'tienda de campaña'. In Latin America you will also hear 'el negocio'.

cards.nota: O 'j' espanhol tem som de 'r' forte do português.
cards.notaEn: 'El pájaro' is a small bird; 'el ave' is the wider word, taking in eagles and hens alike. The Spanish j rasps at the back of the throat.

cards.nota: Falso amigo. Carpete = 'moqueta' ou 'alfombra'.
cards.notaEn: 'La carpeta' is a folder, on a desk or on a screen. A carpet is 'la moqueta' or 'la alfombra' — the resemblance is a trap.

cards.nota: Falso amigo. Firma (empresa) = 'empresa'. E 'firmar' = assinar.
cards.notaEn: 'La firma' is the signature, and 'firmar' is to sign. A firm in the business sense is 'la empresa', though 'la firma' can stretch that way in formal writing.

cards.nota: Vem de 'nieve' (neve). Também se diz 'frigorífico' na Espanha.
cards.notaEn: From 'la nieve', snow. In Spain you will also hear 'el frigorífico'; in Latin America, 'el refrigerador' or 'la heladera'.

cards.nota: Na América Latina também se diz 'la llave' ou 'el caño'.
cards.notaEn: 'El grifo' is the tap — and also the griffin, the beast whose head was carved on old fountains. In Latin America the tap is 'la llave' or 'el caño'.

cards.nota: 'Sacar la basura' = levar o lixo para fora.
cards.notaEn: 'Sacar la basura' = to take the rubbish out. The bin is 'el cubo de la basura' in Spain, 'el bote' or 'el tacho' elsewhere.

cards.en: to be in the habit of
aceitasEn: to be in the habit of
cards.nota: Verbo sem equivalente direto: 'suelo ir' = costumo ir. Muito frequente.
cards.notaEn: Spanish packs 'usually' into a verb: 'suelo ir' = I usually go, 'solía ir' = I used to go. English has no equivalent verb, so it comes out as an adverb instead.

cards.nota: 'Me enteré ayer' = fiquei sabendo ontem.
cards.notaEn: 'Me enteré ayer' = I found out yesterday. '¿Te enteras?' is do you get it — and '¡no me entero!' is the cry of someone lost in a conversation.

cards.nota: De 'atascarse' (entupir, emperrar). Também: 'embotellamiento'.
cards.notaEn: From 'atascarse', to get stuck or clogged; it also names a blockage in a pipe. In Latin America you would say 'el embotellamiento' or 'el trancón'.

cards.nota: 'Estar en huelga' = estar em greve. Cuidado: 'folga' = 'descanso'.
cards.notaEn: 'Estar en huelga' = to be on strike. It comes from 'holgar', to rest or be idle, which also gives 'holgazán', a layabout.

cards.nota: 'Retar a alguien' = desafiar alguém.
cards.notaEn: 'Un reto' is a challenge, and 'retar a alguien' is to challenge them. In the Southern Cone 'retar' also means to tell someone off.

cards.nota: '¿Cuánto tardas?' = quanto tempo você demora?
cards.notaEn: '¿Cuánto tardas?' = how long will you be? It measures duration, not lateness — to arrive late is 'llegar tarde'.

cards.nota: 'Un hito histórico' = um marco histórico.
cards.notaEn: 'Un hito histórico' = a historic milestone. The original 'hito' was the boundary stone driven into the ground to mark a limit.

cards.nota: 'Sesgo cognitivo' = viés cognitivo. Também: corte na diagonal.
cards.notaEn: 'Sesgo cognitivo' = cognitive bias. Its first meaning is a slant or a diagonal cut, and the figurative sense grew straight out of it.

cards.nota: 'En pleno auge' = no auge.
cards.notaEn: 'En pleno auge' = at its height. It also names an economic boom: 'el auge de los años veinte'.

cards.nota: 'Brecha salarial' = diferença salarial.
cards.notaEn: 'Brecha salarial' = the pay gap. Its first sense is a breach in a wall, and 'seguir en la brecha' means to still be in the thick of it.

cards.nota: 'Plantear una pregunta' = fazer uma pergunta. 'Plantearse' = considerar.
cards.notaEn: 'Plantear una pregunta' = to raise a question; 'plantear un problema' is to set one out. Reflexive, 'plantearse' is to consider doing something.

cards.nota: Tédio profundo, com um quê de repulsa. De 'hastiar'.
cards.notaEn: 'El hastío' is boredom gone sour — tedium with a curl of disgust in it. From 'hastiar', to sicken. Heavier than plain 'aburrimiento'.

cards.nota: 'Una idea descabellada' = uma ideia sem pé nem cabeça.
cards.notaEn: 'Una idea descabellada' = a wild, half-baked idea. Literally hairless, as though the thing had lost its head.

cards.nota: 'Una necesidad acuciante' = uma necessidade premente.
cards.notaEn: 'Una necesidad acuciante' = a pressing need. From 'acuciar', to urge on — the word has a push behind it.

cards.nota: Literalmente 'rangendo os dentes'. Fazer algo sem querer.
cards.notaEn: Literally with grinding teeth: doing the thing while making plain you would rather not. 'Aceptó a regañadientes'.

cards.nota: Esperteza com má intenção. Não confundir com 'teimoso' = 'tozudo'.
cards.notaEn: 'Taimado' is cleverness with bad intent — cunning that is planning something. Plain stubbornness is 'tozudo'.

cards.nota: Na Espanha é pejorativo (longo demais); no Cone Sul pode ser elogio (caprichado).
cards.notaEn: In Spain 'prolijo' is a complaint: it goes on far too long. In Argentina and Uruguay it flips into praise — neat, tidy, carefully done.

cards.nota: 'Un rostro adusto' = um rosto fechado, sem simpatia.
cards.notaEn: 'Un rostro adusto' = a stern, closed face. It describes manner more than character: severe, unsmiling, hard to approach.

cards.nota: Também no sentido figurado: 'soterrar un proyecto' = engavetar um projeto.
cards.notaEn: 'Soterrar' is to put underground — cables, pipes, a body. Figuratively it buries a project or a piece of news: 'soterrar el informe'.

cards.nota: 'Llamarse' = chamar-se. Resposta: 'me llamo…'.
cards.notaEn: 'Llamarse' is literally to call oneself. The answer comes back in the same shape: 'me llamo Ana'.

distratoresEn: Where does the bath come from?

cards.nota: Na América Latina se diz mais 'el baño'; na Espanha, 'el servicio'.
cards.notaEn: In Latin America ask for 'el baño'; in Spain, 'el servicio' or 'los aseos'. In a bar, '¿dónde están los servicios?' is the polite version.

cards.notaEn: 'Entender' and 'comprender' both work here. The double negative is compulsory: 'no entiendo nada', never 'entiendo nada'.

cards.nota: 'Costar' também significa 'ser difícil': 'me cuesta entenderlo'.
cards.notaEn: 'Costar' also means to be hard: 'me cuesta entenderlo' = I find it hard to understand. Same verb, quite a different bill.

cards.nota: Em espanhol se 'tem' fome; em português se 'está com' fome.
cards.notaEn: Spanish has hunger rather than being hungry: 'tengo hambre', 'tengo sed', 'tengo frío', 'tengo sueño'. Learn the pattern once and it covers all of them.

cards.nota: 'Mañana' é amanhã; 'la mañana' é a manhã. O artigo muda tudo.
cards.notaEn: 'Mañana' with no article is tomorrow; 'la mañana' with one is the morning. 'Mañana por la mañana' = tomorrow morning, and it is not a joke.

cards.nota: Cuidado com 'acordar', que em espanhol é combinar, não despertar.
cards.notaEn: 'Estar de acuerdo' = to agree. 'Un acuerdo' is an agreement and 'acordar' is to agree on something — not to wake up, which is 'despertarse'.

cards.nota: Par do card 'acordarse': lembrar-se, e não despertar.
cards.notaEn: 'Acordarse de' = to remember. Reflexive, and with 'de': 'no me acuerdo de su nombre'. The plain verb 'acordar' means something else entirely.

cards.notaEn: 'Echar una mano' is to help out, not to hold out a hand. Taking someone's hand is 'dar la mano'.

cards.notaEn: 'A cántaros' = by the pitcherful. Spanish pours water where English drops animals, and both mean the same downpour.

cards.nota: Resposta comum: 'no te preocupes, no pasa nada'.
cards.notaEn: 'Preocuparse' is reflexive: you worry yourself. The full reassurance runs 'no te preocupes, no pasa nada'.

cards.notaEn: 'Soler + infinitive' carries the 'usually' inside the verb. English has to spell it out with an adverb; Spanish just conjugates 'soler'.

cards.notaEn: 'Apetecer' works backwards, like 'gustar': the coffee appeals to you. Very Spanish — in Latin America you would hear '¿se te antoja un café?'

cards.notaEn: 'Tardar en + infinitive' = to take time to do something. 'Tardé dos horas' says how long it took, with no complaint about lateness attached.

aceitasEn: i have a knack for cooking

cards.notaEn: 'Dársele bien algo a alguien' = to be good at something, with the skill doing the giving: cooking goes well for me. Its opposite is 'se me da mal'.

To close the account, it doesn't matter.
cards.nota: Conector muito usado para concluir um raciocínio.
cards.notaEn: 'A fin de cuentas' is the connector that wraps an argument up: when the accounts are settled. Its neighbours are 'al fin y al cabo' and 'en definitiva'.

cards.notaEn: 'Por lo visto' = by all appearances, apparently. It hedges: you are reporting how things look, not what you know.

Counting on you coming, I will go.

Tell me you will come, I don't mind.

cards.notaEn: 'Con tal de que' + subjunctive = as long as, provided that. The whole point is the condition, so the subjunctive is not optional.

cards.es: Dicho sea de paso, tenía razón.

cards.notaEn: 'Dicho sea de paso' = let it be said in passing. A fixed formula with the subjunctive frozen inside it, used to slip a remark in sideways.

cards.notaEn: A compliment: there is nothing in it you would throw away. Said of a book, a film, a speech — good all the way through.

cards.notaEn: 'Irse de rositas' = to walk away from a deserved punishment with nothing sticking to you at all. Spanish, and heavy with resentment.

cards.notaEn: 'Gato encerrado' = a cat shut away where you cannot see it. Somebody is hiding something, and you can tell.

cards.notaEn: 'Habida cuenta de' = in view of, taking into account. Formal and legal register; you will meet it in rulings and reports, not in the bar.

cards.nota: 'So' aqui é 'sob', preposição arcaica que sobrevive em fórmulas jurídicas.
cards.notaEn: 'So' here is an archaic 'bajo', under. It survives only in frozen legal formulas: 'so pena de', 'so pretexto de'.

cards.notaEn: 'A la sazón' = at that time. Literary and dated. 'La sazón' on its own is seasoning, and 'sazonar' is to season food — the two senses have drifted a long way apart.

distratoresEn: Yesterday I did not know it.

cards.notaEn: 'Saber' shifts meaning in the preterite: 'supe' is not I knew but I found out, the moment the knowledge arrived. The imperfect 'sabía' is the ongoing state.

cards.notaEn: 'Hacer' in the preterite: hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron. Watch the z in 'hizo' — it keeps the sound when the vowel changes.

cards.notaEn: 'Hago' with a g, like 'tengo', 'pongo', 'salgo', 'digo'. The g shows up only in the first person singular; the rest of the present is regular.

cards.notaEn: 'Ir' has one of only three irregular imperfects in Spanish: iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban. The other two belong to 'ser' and 'ver'.

cards.notaEn: 'Decir': dije, dijiste, dijo, dijimos, dijisteis, dijeron. Note 'dijeron' with no i — after a j, the i of the ending drops away.

cards.nota: 'Decir' no presente muda o e por i: digo, dices, dice, decimos, decís, dicen.
cards.notaEn: 'Decir' changes e to i in the present: digo, dices, dice, decimos, decís, dicen. The 'nosotros' and 'vosotros' forms keep the e.

cards.nota: Pega muita gente: 'andar' é irregular no pretérito — anduve, anduviste, anduvo.
cards.notaEn: This one catches people out: 'andar' looks regular and is not. The preterite runs anduve, anduviste, anduvo — the same -uv- as 'tener' and 'estar'.

distratoresEn: He used to bring the book.

cards.notaEn: 'Traer': traje, trajiste, trajo, trajimos, trajisteis, trajeron. Like 'dijeron', the third person plural drops the i after the j.

cards.notaEn: 'Ver': vi, viste, vio, vimos, visteis, vieron. 'Vi' and 'vio' carry no written accent, unlike most preterites of their shape.

cards.nota: 'Ver' tem imperfeito irregular: veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veíais, veían.
cards.notaEn: 'Ver' keeps the e of its stem in the imperfect: veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veíais, veían. One of the three irregular imperfects, alongside 'ser' and 'ir'.

cards.nota: 'Salgo' com g. O futuro também é irregular: saldré.
cards.notaEn: 'Salgo' with a g, like 'tengo' and 'pongo'. The future is irregular too: saldré, saldrás, saldrá.

cards.nota: Verbos em -cer ganham z: conozco, parezco, agradezco, merezco.
cards.notaEn: Verbs in -cer take a z in the first person: conozco, parezco, agradezco, merezco. And 'conocer' is knowing a person; 'saber' is knowing a fact.

cards.nota: 'Oír': oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen. O y aparece do nada.
cards.notaEn: 'Oír': oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen. A y appears from nowhere in the middle of the paradigm. Listening on purpose is 'escuchar'.

cards.nota: Na 3ª pessoa o o vira u: durmió, durmieron. No presente vira ue: duermo.
cards.notaEn: In the third person of the preterite the o turns into u: durmió, durmieron. In the present it turns into ue instead: duermo.

cards.nota: Mudança o→ue: duermo, duermes, duerme, dormimos, dormís, duermen.
cards.notaEn: An o→ue stem change: duermo, duermes, duerme, dormimos, dormís, duermen. The 'nosotros' and 'vosotros' forms keep the plain o.

distratoresEn: He used to ask for the bill.
He will ask for the bill.
He would ask for the bill.
cards.nota: Na 3ª pessoa o e vira i: pidió, pidieron. Cuidado: 'pedir' não é 'perguntar'.
cards.notaEn: In the third person of the preterite the e becomes i: pidió, pidieron. And 'pedir' is to ask for something; asking a question is 'preguntar'.

cards.nota: Único verbo com u→ue: juego, juegas, juega, jugamos, jugáis, juegan.
cards.notaEn: 'Jugar' is the only Spanish verb with a u→ue change: juego, juegas, juega, jugamos, jugáis, juegan. Note the 'al': 'jugar al fútbol'.

cards.nota: Mudança e→ie: empiezo, empiezas, empieza. No pretérito: empecé, com c.
cards.notaEn: An e→ie change: empiezo, empiezas, empieza. In the preterite the z turns into a c to keep the sound: 'empecé'.

distratoresEn: I hope he is coming tomorrow.
I hope he will come tomorrow.
I hope he would come tomorrow.
cards.nota: Presente do subjuntivo de 'venir' sai do 'vengo': venga, vengas, venga.
cards.notaEn: The present subjunctive of 'venir' is built off 'vengo': venga, vengas, venga. 'Ojalá' always takes the subjunctive — with the present it is a real hope, with the imperfect a wish you do not expect to be granted.

formasEs.Ojalá viene mañana: indicativo, onde o subjuntivo é obrigatório
formasEs.Ojalá vendrá mañana: futuro do indicativo, que aqui não cabe

formasEsEn.Ojalá viene mañana: indicative, where the subjunctive is required
formasEsEn.Ojalá vendrá mañana: future indicative, which does not fit here

cards.notaEn: 'Ser' in the present subjunctive: sea, seas, sea, seamos, seáis, sean. 'No creer que' triggers the subjunctive; a plain 'creo que' does not.

formasEs.No creo que es fácil: indicativo, onde o subjuntivo é obrigatório

distratoresEn: When you have the time now.
When you used to have time.
cards.nota: Futuro incerto pede subjuntivo nas duas línguas: 'cuando tengas' = quando tiver.
cards.notaEn: 'Cuando' pointing at an uncertain future takes the subjunctive: 'cuando tengas tiempo'. Pointing at a habit, it takes the indicative: 'cuando tienes tiempo, lees'.

cards.nota: Imperativos curtos e irregulares: ven, ten, haz, di, sal, pon, sé, ve.
cards.notaEn: Spanish keeps a short irregular imperative for its commonest verbs: ven, ten, haz, di, sal, pon, sé, ve. All one syllable, and worth memorising as a set.

distratoresEn: He used to do what he wanted!
He will do what he wants!
He would do what he wanted!
cards.nota: 'Haz' é o imperativo de 'hacer'. Note o subjuntivo 'quieras' depois.
cards.notaEn: 'Haz' is the imperative of 'hacer'. Note the subjunctive that follows: 'lo que quieras', whatever you may want, because the wanting is left open.

If I had money, I travelled.

I have money, so I travel.
cards.nota: Imperfeito do subjuntivo + condicional, igual ao português.
cards.notaEn: The unreal conditional: imperfect subjunctive in the 'si' clause, conditional in the other. Never a future after 'si' — 'si tendré' is simply ungrammatical.

distratoresEn: I had come earlier than that.
cards.nota: 'Haber' no condicional: habría, habrías, habría. Serve para o 'teria feito'.
cards.notaEn: 'Haber' in the conditional: habría, habrías, habría. With a past participle it builds the conditional perfect — the thing that would have happened and did not.

cards.nota: Regular em -ar: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan.
cards.notaEn: A model regular -ar verb: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan. Learn this one and thousands of others come free.

cards.nota: Regular em -er: comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron.
cards.notaEn: A regular -er verb in the preterite: comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron. Only the first and third persons carry a written accent.

cards.nota: Em -ir, presente e pretérito de 'nosotros' são iguais: vivimos. O contexto decide.
cards.notaEn: In -ir verbs the 'nosotros' present and preterite are the same word: 'vivimos' is both we live and we lived. Only context tells them apart.

aceitasEn: i used to work a lot
i worked a lot back then
i would work a lot in those days
cards.nota: Imperfeito regular em -ar: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban.
cards.notaEn: The regular -ar imperfect: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban. It describes what used to go on, with no beginning or end in view.

aceitasEn: they are going to study tomorrow
cards.nota: O futuro regular junta a terminação ao infinitivo inteiro: estudar + án.
cards.notaEn: The regular future glues the ending onto the whole infinitive: estudiar + án. That is why every form but 'nosotros' carries a written accent.

aceitasEn: i could go for a coffee
distratoresEn: I used to have a coffee.
cards.nota: Condicional regular: infinitivo + ía. Em português usamos mais 'tomar' que 'beber'.
cards.notaEn: The regular conditional adds -ía to the full infinitive: beber + ía. The same endings serve -ar, -er and -ir alike.

cards.nota: O espanhol usa muito o 'he/has/ha/hemos + particípio' onde o português usa o passado simples.
cards.notaEn: 'He/has/ha/hemos + participle' is the present perfect, and Spain reaches for it constantly for anything that happened today. Latin America leans on the simple preterite instead.

cards.nota: Gerúndio em -ando/-iendo. Igual ao português, mas o espanhol usa menos.
cards.notaEn: The gerund ends in -ando or -iendo. Spanish uses the continuous far less than English does: 'como a las dos' already covers I'm eating at two.

cards.nota: 'Gustar' inverte: quem gosta vira objeto indireto. 'Me gusta' = a mim agrada.
cards.notaEn: 'Gustar' runs backwards: the thing liked is the subject and you are the indirect object. 'Me gusta esperar' is literally waiting pleases me.

cards.pt: O copo caiu da minha mão.
aceitas: o copo caiu da minha mao
caiu o copo da minha mao
aceitasEn: the glass slipped out of my hand
i dropped the glass by accident
the glass fell out of my hand
distratores: Eu enchi o copo de novo.
cards.nota: O 'se me' tira a culpa: não foi você que derrubou, aconteceu. E 'vaso' = copo.
cards.notaEn: 'Se me cayó' takes the blame off you: the glass fell on me, it was not my doing. Saying 'tiré el vaso' would admit you threw it. And 'el vaso' is a drinking glass.

cards.nota: Par de 'borracho' (bêbado). Aqui o material é 'goma'; na América Latina, 'borrador'.
cards.notaEn: 'Goma' is the rubber itself, so 'goma de borrar' is the thing you rub out with. In Latin America it is 'el borrador' — which in Spain means a rough draft.

cards.nota: 'Cola' em espanhol é rabo ou fila. A cola de colar é 'pegamento'.
cards.notaEn: From 'pegar', to stick. Watch out for 'la cola', which in Spanish is a tail or a queue, never the stuff in the tube.

cards.nota: Par de 'vaso' (copo). O vaso de flores é 'jarrón' ou 'florero'.
cards.notaEn: 'El jarrón' is the ornamental vase; 'el florero' is the one you actually put flowers in. Neither is 'el vaso', which you drink from.

cards.nota: Par de 'un rato' (um tempinho). O animal é 'ratón' — e o do computador também.
cards.notaEn: 'El ratón' is the mouse, animal or computer alike. The bigger rat is 'la rata'. And 'un rato', with no n, is a short while.

cards.nota: Par de 'aula' (sala). A aula em si é 'clase'.
cards.notaEn: 'La clase' is the lesson, and also the kind or sort of a thing: '¿qué clase de pregunta es esa?'. The room it happens in is 'el aula'.

cards.nota: Par de 'crianza' (criação). Criança é 'niño' ou 'niña'.
cards.notaEn: 'El niño' is a boy, 'la niña' a girl, 'los niños' children of either sort. The raising of them is 'la crianza'.

cards.nota: Par de 'propina' (gorjeta). O suborno é 'soborno'.
cards.notaEn: 'El soborno' is the bribe and 'sobornar' is to bribe. Keep it well apart from 'la propina', the tip you leave a waiter.

cards.nota: Par de 'presunto' (suposto). O embutido é 'jamón'.
cards.notaEn: 'El jamón' is ham, and in Spain a national obsession: 'jamón serrano', 'jamón ibérico'. Nothing to do with 'presunto', which means alleged.

cards.nota: Par de 'acordarse' (lembrar-se). Acordar do sono é 'despertarse'.
cards.notaEn: 'Despertarse' is to wake up; 'despertar' without the pronoun is to wake somebody else. Do not reach for 'acordarse', which is to remember.

cards.nota: Par de 'cena' (jantar). A cena de filme é 'escena'.
cards.notaEn: 'La escena' is the scene of a film or a crime, and 'el escenario' is the stage. Watch the e at the front: without it, 'la cena' is dinner.

cards.nota: Par de 'apellido' (sobrenome). O apelido é 'apodo' ou 'sobrenombre'.
cards.notaEn: 'El apodo' is the nickname; 'el apellido' is the family name. Latin America also says 'el sobrenombre' for the nickname.

cards.nota: Não confunda com 'salida' (saída). E sucesso em espanhol não é 'suceso'.
cards.notaEn: 'El éxito' is success — the exit is 'la salida', and the resemblance has embarrassed many travellers. 'Tener éxito' = to succeed.

cards.nota: Falso amigo perigoso: 'suceso' é acontecimento, às vezes ruim. Sucesso é 'éxito'.
cards.notaEn: 'Un suceso' is an event, often an unpleasant one — the crime pages of a Spanish paper are 'la sección de sucesos'. Success is 'el éxito'.

cards.nota: 'Llevarse un disgusto' = levar um desgosto. Não é 'nojo', que é 'asco'.
cards.notaEn: 'Llevarse un disgusto' = to get bad news, to be upset. It is annoyance and distress, not revulsion — disgust in that sense is 'el asco'.

cards.nota: Par de 'vaso' (copo). A taça é 'copa' — e a Copa do Mundo também.
cards.notaEn: 'Una copa' is a stemmed glass, and 'tomar una copa' is to go out for a drink. It is also the trophy: 'la Copa del Mundo'.

cards.nota: 'Tasa de interés' = taxa de juros. Não confunda com 'taza' (xícara).
cards.notaEn: 'Tasa de interés' = interest rate; 'tasa de paro' = unemployment rate. One letter away sits 'la taza', a cup — and they sound identical across most of the Spanish world.

cards.nota: Par de 'sobremesa' (conversa após a refeição). O doce é 'postre'.
cards.notaEn: 'De postre' = for dessert. It is what comes after the meal, whereas 'la sobremesa' is the talk that comes after that.

cards.nota: 'Techo' é o teto; o telhado por fora é 'tejado'.
cards.notaEn: 'El techo' is the ceiling you see from inside; 'el tejado' is the roof you see from the street. Figuratively it is also a ceiling on prices.

cards.nota: Muro externo é 'muro'; parede de dentro é 'pared'.
cards.notaEn: 'La pared' is an interior wall; 'el muro' is the outside one that surrounds a property; 'la muralla' is the wall around a city.

cards.nota: Lembre que 'cadera' é quadril. 'Silla' é a cadeira de sentar.
cards.notaEn: 'La silla' is the chair you sit on, and 'el sillón' the armchair. Do not confuse it with 'la cadera', which is your hip.

cards.nota: Talheres: cuchillo (faca), tenedor (garfo), cuchara (colher).
cards.notaEn: The place setting: 'cuchillo' the knife, 'tenedor' the fork, 'cuchara' the spoon. All three together are 'los cubiertos'.

cards.nota: De 'tener' (segurar). Cuidado: 'cubierto' é o talher em geral.
cards.notaEn: From 'tener', to hold: the fork is the holder. In finance the same word means a holder of securities — 'el tenedor de bonos'.

cards.nota: A colher de chá é 'cucharita' ou 'cucharilla'.
cards.notaEn: 'La cuchara' is the spoon, and the small one is 'la cucharita' or 'la cucharilla'. A spoonful is 'una cucharada'.

cards.nota: De 'servir'. Nada a ver com 'servil'.
cards.notaEn: From 'servir', to serve. The paper one is 'una servilleta de papel'; the cloth one, 'de tela'.

cards.nota: Na Espanha é 'zumo'; na América Latina, 'jugo'.
cards.notaEn: In Spain, 'zumo de naranja'. Across Latin America it is 'el jugo' — ask for 'zumo' in Mexico and you may get a puzzled look.

cards.nota: Na América Latina se diz 'durazno'.
cards.notaEn: 'El melocotón' in Spain, 'el durazno' across most of Latin America. Both mean the same fruit; the word marks where you learned your Spanish.

cards.nota: Vem do formato de pinha. 'Piña colada' é literalmente abacaxi coado.
cards.notaEn: Named for its resemblance to a pine cone, which is also 'una piña'. 'Piña colada' is literally strained pineapple.

cards.nota: Do árabe. Não confunda com 'sandalia' (sandália).
cards.notaEn: An Arabic borrowing, from 'sindiyya', the fruit of Sindh. Keep it apart from 'la sandalia', which goes on your foot.

cards.nota: Na Argentina e no Uruguai se diz 'manteca'.
cards.notaEn: 'La mantequilla' in Spain and most of Latin America; in Argentina and Uruguay it is 'la manteca', which elsewhere means lard.

cards.nota: Cuidado com 'polvo' (pó) e 'pulpo' (polvo). 'Pollo' é frango.
cards.notaEn: Three lookalikes to keep straight: 'el pollo' is chicken, 'el polvo' is dust, 'el pulpo' is octopus. Mixing them up makes for memorable menus.

cards.nota: Cuidado: 'consejo' é conselho. 'Conejo' é o bicho.
cards.notaEn: Careful with 'el consejo', which is advice or a council. One letter and one syllable away from the animal.

cards.nota: Também vira adjetivo: 'ser un zorro' = ser esperto.
cards.notaEn: 'El zorro' is the fox, and 'ser un zorro' is to be a sly one. The female, 'la zorra', is far coarser as an insult — use with care.

cards.nota: Cuidado: 'oveja' é ovelha. Uma letra separa as duas.
cards.notaEn: One letter separates 'la abeja', the bee, from 'la oveja', the sheep. The hive is 'la colmena' and honey is 'la miel'.

cards.nota: Também é o nado borboleta.
cards.notaEn: 'La mariposa' is the butterfly, and also the butterfly stroke in swimming. A moth is 'la polilla'.

cards.nota: O f- do português virou h- mudo em espanhol: formiga/hormiga, fazer/hacer.
cards.notaEn: Latin f- turned into a silent Spanish h-: formica became 'hormiga', facere became 'hacer', filius became 'hijo'. The h is written and never pronounced.

cards.nota: O 'ñ' faz o som do nosso 'nh'.
cards.notaEn: The ñ is a letter in its own right, with its own place in the alphabet, sounding like the ni in onion. A spider's web is 'una telaraña'.

cards.nota: 'Bolsa' é a bolsa; 'bolsillo' é o bolso da roupa.
cards.notaEn: 'El bolsillo' is the pocket in your clothes; 'el bolso' is a handbag and 'la bolsa' a bag or the stock exchange. The -illo ending is a diminutive.

cards.nota: 'Cinturón de seguridad' = cinto de segurança.
cards.notaEn: 'Cinturón de seguridad' = seat belt. 'La cintura' is the waist it goes around, and 'apretarse el cinturón' tightens the belt in the money sense too.

cards.nota: Vem de 'croata', pelo lenço que os croatas usavam no pescoço.
cards.notaEn: From 'croata', Croat: the scarf Croatian soldiers wore at the neck gave Europe the necktie. A bow tie is 'una pajarita'.

cards.nota: Meia-calça é 'medias' — justamente o falso amigo.
cards.notaEn: 'Los calcetines' are socks. Watch out for 'las medias', which are stockings or tights — though in parts of Latin America they mean socks after all.

cards.nota: Na América Latina se diz 'lentes' ou 'anteojos'.
cards.notaEn: 'Las gafas' in Spain; 'los lentes' or 'los anteojos' across Latin America. Sunglasses are 'las gafas de sol'.

cards.nota: Literalmente 'para águas'. O de sol é 'sombrilla'.
cards.notaEn: Literally stop-waters, built like 'parabrisas' and 'paracaídas'. The one you carry against the sun is 'la sombrilla'.

cards.nota: O mesmo 'j' com som de r forte. Sabão em pó é 'detergente'.
cards.notaEn: 'El jabón' is soap, and the j rasps at the back of the throat. Washing powder is 'el detergente'.

cards.nota: 'Darse una ducha' = tomar banho.
cards.notaEn: 'Darse una ducha' or plain 'ducharse' = to have a shower. The bath you lie in is 'la bañera'.

cards.nota: O 'j' espanhol soa como r forte: es-pe-ro.
cards.notaEn: 'El espejo' is the mirror. Note the Spanish habit of putting an e in front of s + consonant: espejo, escuela, España, especial.

cards.nota: Do árabe, como quase toda palavra espanhola que começa com 'al-'.
cards.notaEn: Arabic, like nearly every Spanish word beginning in al-: almohada, almacén, alcalde, algodón. Eight centuries of Al-Andalus left them behind.

cards.nota: Acento na primeira sílaba: SÁ-ba-na. 'Sabana' sem acento é savana.
cards.notaEn: Stress on the first syllable: SÁ-ba-na. Move it and you get 'sabana', the savannah — the written accent is the only thing keeping them apart.

cards.nota: Caixão de defunto é 'ataúd'. 'Cajón' é a gaveta.
cards.notaEn: 'El cajón' is a drawer, and 'la caja' the box it grew out of. A coffin is 'el ataúd'. In the Andes a 'cajón' can also be a narrow gorge.

cards.nota: 'Tener enchufe' também significa ter pistolão, ter QI.
cards.notaEn: 'El enchufe' is the socket and 'enchufar' is to plug in. Figuratively, 'tener enchufe' means having connections in the right places.

cards.nota: Na Argentina, 'bombilla' é o canudo do chimarrão.
cards.notaEn: 'La bombilla' is the light bulb in Spain; in Latin America you may hear 'el foco' or 'la bombita'. In Argentina a 'bombilla' is the metal straw for mate.

cards.nota: 'Mando a distancia'. Também significa comando, chefia.
cards.notaEn: Short for 'mando a distancia'. On its own, 'el mando' is command or authority: 'estar al mando' is to be in charge.

cards.nota: De 'cerrar' (fechar). Serragem é 'serrín'.
cards.notaEn: From 'cerrar', to close. The key that opens it is 'la llave', and the keyhole is 'el ojo de la cerradura' — the eye of the lock.

cards.nota: 'Le falta un tornillo' = falta um parafuso, é meio doido.
cards.notaEn: 'Le falta un tornillo' = he's got a screw loose. A nut is 'la tuerca' and a screwdriver is 'el destornillador'.

cards.nota: Mesmo padrão de 'tornillo', 'bolsillo': o -illo é diminutivo.
cards.notaEn: The same -illo ending as 'tornillo' and 'bolsillo' — originally a diminutive, long since frozen into the word itself.

cards.nota: Cuidado: ladrilho de piso é 'baldosa' ou 'azulejo'.
cards.notaEn: 'El ladrillo' is a building brick. A floor or wall tile is 'la baldosa' or 'el azulejo'. Careful with 'el ladrón', the thief.

cards.nota: De 'ascender'. Na Colômbia e no México se diz 'elevador'.
cards.notaEn: From 'ascender', to go up. Spain says 'el ascensor'; Mexico and Colombia say 'el elevador'.

cards.nota: Na Argentina, 'vereda'. No México, 'banqueta'.
cards.notaEn: 'La acera' in Spain, 'la vereda' in Argentina, 'la banqueta' in Mexico. Same strip of concrete, three different words.

cards.nota: 'Barro' em espanhol é lama. O bairro é 'barrio'.
cards.notaEn: 'El barrio' is your neighbourhood, and it carries real warmth: 'la gente del barrio'. Careful with 'el barro', which is mud or clay.

cards.nota: 'Buzón de voz' = caixa postal do telefone.
cards.notaEn: 'El buzón' is the postbox on the street or the letterbox at your door. 'Buzón de voz' is a voicemail box.

cards.nota: A plataforma da estação de trem ou metrô.
cards.notaEn: 'El andén' is the platform at a railway or metro station: 'el tren sale del andén cuatro'. In Colombia it also means the pavement.

cards.nota: 'Hacer la maleta' = fazer as malas.
cards.notaEn: 'Hacer la maleta' = to pack. The small one is 'el maletín', a briefcase, and the car boot in Spain is 'el maletero'.

cards.nota: Cuidado: 'equipo' é equipe ou equipamento. 'Equipaje' é bagagem.
cards.notaEn: Careful with 'el equipo', which is a team or a set of equipment. 'El equipaje' is only what you travel with: 'equipaje de mano' is hand luggage.

cards.nota: Na América Latina, 'plomero'. De 'fontana' (fonte).
cards.notaEn: From 'fontana', a spring or fountain. Spain says 'fontanero'; most of Latin America says 'plomero', after the lead in old pipes.

cards.nota: Do árabe 'al-banni' (construtor).
cards.notaEn: Arabic again, from 'al-bannā', the builder. It covers bricklayers and general builders alike.

cards.nota: De 'cerradura' (fechadura). O objeto chaveiro é 'llavero'.
cards.notaEn: From 'la cerradura', the lock. The keyring you carry is 'el llavero' — different word, same trade.

cards.nota: Também 'salario'. 'Sueldo mínimo' = salário mínimo.
cards.notaEn: 'El sueldo' is the wage you draw each month; 'el salario' works too, and 'el sueldo mínimo' is the minimum wage.

cards.nota: 'Jubilarse' = aposentar-se. Vem de júbilo, a alegria de parar.
cards.notaEn: 'Jubilarse' = to retire. It shares a root with 'júbilo', joy — the language is optimistic about the moment you stop.

cards.nota: 'Estar en el paro' = estar desempregado. Também significa paralisação.
cards.notaEn: 'Estar en el paro' = to be out of work, in Spain. It also means a stoppage or a strike: 'un paro general'. Latin America says 'el desempleo'.

cards.nota: Cuidado: 'despedida' é a despedida. 'Despido' é ser demitido.
cards.notaEn: 'El despido' is being sacked; 'despedir a alguien' is to fire them. Careful with 'la despedida', which is a goodbye — and 'despedirse' is to say one.

cards.nota: 'Becario' é o bolsista, e também o estagiário.
cards.notaEn: 'Una beca' is a grant or scholarship, and 'un becario' is the person on one — which in Spain also means an intern, often unpaid.

cards.nota: De 'borrar' (apagar). Na América Latina também é a borracha de apagar.
cards.notaEn: From 'borrar', to rub out — a draft is what you will still be erasing. In Latin America the same word also names the rubber you erase with.

cards.nota: Também é o titular de um cargo ou de uma conta.
cards.notaEn: 'El titular' is a newspaper headline, and also the holder of a post or an account: 'el titular de la cuenta'. As a verb it means to entitle.

cards.nota: Também é o hífen na escrita. 'Guionista' é o roteirista.
cards.notaEn: 'El guion' is a film or television script, and 'el guionista' the writer of it. In punctuation the same word means a hyphen.

cards.nota: De 'estrenar' (usar pela primeira vez), que já apareceu como verbo.
cards.notaEn: 'El estreno' is the opening night. It comes from 'estrenar', to use something for the very first time — a film, a pair of shoes, a flat.

cards.nota: De 'girar', rodar. 'Estar de gira' = estar em turnê.
cards.notaEn: From 'girar', to turn or go round. 'Estar de gira' = to be on tour. A sightseeing tour is 'una visita' or 'un recorrido' instead.

cards.nota: 'Repunte económico' = retomada da economia. O oposto é 'caída'.
cards.notaEn: 'Repunte económico' = economic upturn. It marks a rise after a fall; the opposite is 'la caída'.

cards.nota: Serve para prédio que cai e para bolsa que despenca.
cards.notaEn: 'El desplome' works for a building coming down and for a market falling out of the sky: 'el desplome de la bolsa'.

cards.nota: Cuidado com a grafia: injerencia com j, de 'injerir' (intrometer-se).
cards.notaEn: Spelled with a j, from 'injerirse', to meddle. 'Injerencia extranjera' = foreign interference. Do not confuse it with 'ingerir', to swallow.

cards.nota: De 'atajar' (cortar caminho). Não confunda com 'ataque'.
cards.notaEn: From 'atajar', to cut across. 'Coger un atajo' = to take a shortcut. Careful with 'el ataque', which is an attack.

cards.nota: 'Embustero' é o mentiroso contumaz.
cards.notaEn: 'Un embuste' is a lie built to deceive, more elaborate than a plain 'mentira'. 'Un embustero' is the habitual liar who tells them.

cards.nota: 'Con ahínco' = com afinco. O h é mudo: a-ÍN-co.
cards.notaEn: 'Con ahínco' = with determination, doggedly. The h is silent, as always: a-ÍN-co, with the stress in the middle.

cards.nota: 'Sin mesura' = sem moderação. Não é a mesura de reverência.
cards.notaEn: 'Sin mesura' = without restraint. It names moderation and self-control, not the act of measuring, which is 'la medición'.

cards.nota: 'No es óbice para' = não impede que. Bem formal.
cards.notaEn: Almost always in one formula: 'no es óbice para', it is no bar to. Formal and legal, and rarely met anywhere else.

cards.nota: 'Tenerle inquina a alguien' = ter ojeriza de alguém.
cards.notaEn: 'Tenerle inquina a alguien' = to have it in for somebody. It is a settled, personal dislike, not a passing irritation.

cards.nota: Zombaria cruel, feita em público.
cards.notaEn: 'El escarnio' is cruel mockery made in public, meant to humiliate. Heavier than 'la burla', which can still be affectionate.

cards.nota: 'Sosegado' é o sossegado. Note o -ie- que o português não tem.
cards.notaEn: 'El sosiego' is settled quiet, of a place or of a mind. 'Sosegado' is the person who has it, and 'sosegar' is to calm somebody down.

cards.nota: De 'arrojarse' (lançar-se). 'Arroyo' com y é riacho.
cards.notaEn: From 'arrojarse', to throw oneself in. It is courage of the headlong kind. Spelled with a y, 'el arroyo' is a stream — quite another thing.

cards.nota: Tristeza pesada e duradoura. Mesmo sufixo de 'muchedumbre' (multidão).
cards.notaEn: Grief with weight to it, from 'pesado', heavy — sadness that settles and stays. Same -umbre ending as 'muchedumbre', a crowd.

cards.nota: Estagnação total, sem energia nem movimento.
cards.notaEn: 'El marasmo' is total stagnation, with neither energy nor movement left in it. Used of economies, institutions and moods alike.

cards.nota: Argumento esperto mas falso, feito para enganar.
cards.notaEn: 'Una argucia' is a clever argument that is false on purpose — reasoning bent to deceive. Related to 'agudo', sharp.

cards.nota: 'Remilgos' são os melindres, o fricote.
cards.notaEn: 'Remilgado' is fussy and easily put out, with a show of delicacy about it. 'Los remilgos' are the airs themselves: 'déjate de remilgos'.

cards.nota: 'Una respuesta escueta' = uma resposta seca, sem rodeios.
cards.notaEn: 'Una respuesta escueta' = a bare, curt answer. It means concise, sometimes to the point of coldness — no ornament, no padding.

cards.nota: 'Un día aciago' = um dia funesto, de má sorte.
cards.notaEn: 'Un día aciago' = a fateful, unlucky day. Literary, and always about misfortune: the word carries the omen along with it.

cards.nota: Quem foge do convívio. Não confunda com 'huracán'.
cards.notaEn: 'Huraño' describes the person who avoids company — shyness shading into surliness. The h is silent: u-RA-ño.

cards.nota: 'Acaparar la atención' = monopolizar a atenção.
cards.notaEn: 'Acaparar' is to corner a supply, or to take up more than your share: 'acaparar la atención' is to hog the limelight.

cards.nota: 'Esmerarse en algo' = caprichar em algo. 'Esmero' é o capricho.
cards.notaEn: 'Esmerarse en algo' = to take real care over something, to do it properly. The noun 'el esmero' is that care itself.

cards.nota: 'Rehuir la mirada' = desviar o olhar. O h é mudo: re-u-ÍR.
cards.notaEn: 'Rehuir la mirada' = to avoid someone's eye. The h is silent and the word runs to three syllables: re-u-ÍR.

cards.nota: 'Acatar una orden' = cumprir uma ordem. Cuidado com 'atacar'.
cards.notaEn: 'Acatar una orden' = to obey an order, whether you agree with it or not. Do not let it slide into 'atacar', which is to attack.

cards.nota: Ver de forma vaga, ou pressentir. Combina com 'atisbo'.
cards.notaEn: To make something out faintly, or to sense it coming: 'vislumbrar una solución'. Its noun cousin is 'un atisbo'.

cards.nota: 'Zanjar una discusión' = encerrar de vez uma discussão. De 'zanja' (vala).
cards.notaEn: 'Zanjar una discusión' = to settle an argument for good. From 'una zanja', a ditch — you dig the thing to a close.

cards.es: Se me hace agua la boca.
distratoresEn: I wet my mouth with water.
I drank water through my mouth.
I washed my mouth with water.
cards.nota: Mesma imagem do português, com a construção 'se me' do espanhol.
cards.notaEn: The same picture English uses, built with the Spanish 'se me': the mouth waters on me, with no effort of my own.

distratoresEn: I don't have a good idea.
I did not like that idea.
cards.nota: O 'ni' reforça a negação, como o nosso 'a menor'.
cards.notaEn: 'Ni' sharpens the negative: not so much as an idea. The same trick runs through 'ni un céntimo' and 'ni por asomo'.

distratoresEn: He gave me a nice surprise.
cards.nota: 'Pillar' é o pegar coloquial da Espanha, que já apareceu sozinho.
cards.notaEn: 'Pillar' is the everyday Spanish verb for catching, and 'pillar de sorpresa' is to catch someone off guard.

cards.en: It's good enough to lick your fingers.
aceitasEn: its good enough to lick your fingers
distratoresEn: It is dirty on the fingers.
It is hot on the fingers.
It is stuck to the fingers.
It is glued to the fingers.
cards.nota: Elogio para comida muito boa.
cards.notaEn: 'Para chuparse los dedos' = so good you lick your fingers. Reserved for food, and always a compliment.

cards.es: Le salió el tiro por la culata.
aceitas: o feitico virou contra o feiticeiro
aceitasEn: it blew up in his face
it came back to bite him
distratoresEn: The shot made a lot of noise.
cards.nota: Idêntica ao português: o plano se voltou contra quem o fez.
cards.notaEn: 'La culata' is the butt of a gun: the shot came out of the wrong end. The plan turned on the person who made it.

cards.nota: A construção 'se le' tira a culpa: aconteceu com ele.
cards.notaEn: The 'se le' construction again: it got late on him. Nobody is quite to blame, which is half the point of the form.

distratoresEn: It is sad to watch the attempt.
The penalty is worth the attempt.
cards.nota: 'Valer la pena' = valer a pena, idêntico ao português.
cards.notaEn: 'Valer la pena' = to be worth the trouble. 'La pena' here is the effort or sorrow it costs you, not a punishment.

cards.en: He's had it up to here.
aceitasEn: hes had it up to here
he s had it up to here
hes had it up to the eyeballs
cards.nota: Versão educada de uma expressão bem mais grosseira.
cards.notaEn: 'Hasta las narices' = fed up right up to the nose. It is the polite version of a considerably ruder Spanish phrase.

cards.en: Neither one thing nor the other.
aceitasEn: neither one thing nor the other
it was neither here nor there
cards.nota: Indiferença: nem bom nem ruim, tanto faz.
cards.notaEn: 'Ni fu ni fa' is a shrug: it was neither good nor bad. The two syllables mean nothing on their own — the phrase is pure sound.

aceitasEn: i m too embarrassed to ask
i am too embarrassed to ask
i cant bring myself to ask
distratores: Me obriga a ter que perguntar.
distratoresEn: It irritates me to have to ask.
It costs me a lot to ask.
It really delays me to ask.
It forces me to have to ask.
cards.nota: 'Dar corte' = dar vergonha, na Espanha. 'Cortado' é o envergonhado.
cards.notaEn: 'Dar corte' = to make you feel awkward, in Spain. 'Estar cortado' is to be tongue-tied — and 'un cortado' at the bar is a coffee.

cards.nota: Calcular por estimativa, sem medir. O 'cubero' fazia barris a olho.
cards.notaEn: 'El cubero' was the barrel maker, who sized his casks by eye. The phrase now covers any rough estimate made without measuring.

aceitas: vale mais a manha que a forca
cards.nota: 'Maña' é a habilidade, o jeito. Não confunda com 'mañana'.
cards.notaEn: 'La maña' is skill and knack; 'la fuerza' is raw strength. Do not confuse 'maña' with 'mañana' — one letter and a world apart.
